title: ci: refactor CI workflows, upgrade Node to 18, improve build cache and pin dev deps
author: Jordan Lee
ci_checks: integration-tests: ephemeral infra — passed (flaky on first run, rerun)
description:
Motivation: Our CI workflows were still running on Node 16 images and using an older cache layout which resulted in slow cold CI runs and occasional flakes in the integration step. This PR upgrades workflows to Node 18, consolidates duplicated CI jobs into reusable workflow_call templates, standardizes cache keys for npm/yarn and Docker layer caching, and pins devDependencies used by CI helpers to reduce transient breakages.

What changed (summary): Consolidated .github/workflows/{ci,release,lint}.yml into modular templates under .github/workflows/templates. Switched all matrix jobs to use node-version: 18.x and updated test runners accordingly. Implemented a deterministic cache key scheme: repo-name-{{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}-node-18 and docker-layer-cache keyed by Dockerfile content + base image digest. Pinned a handful of devDeps in package.json used by CI (eslint, jest, ts-node) to avoid silent major upgrades. Introduced scripts/ci-helpers.sh and small helper Dockerfile.ci for reproducible containerized steps used by integration tests.

Checklist: - [x] Upgrade Node runtime in CI to 18.x - [x] Add reusable workflow templates - [x] Implement deterministic cache keys and test cache hits - [x] Pin devDependencies used in CI - [x] Run full CI suite and address flakiness - [x] Update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md for new local CI steps

Testing notes: Initial push saw integration flake due to ephemeral infra teardown timing; adjusted retry backoff and moved testrig teardown to a separate step that runs on job completion. Cache keys were instrumented and verified across multiple runs — subsequent runs show cache hit for node modules and docker layer cache, cutting cold CI time by ~35% in our benchmarks.

Rollout and compatibility: This is a non-breaking infra change. Local contributors using Node 16 will still be able to run the repo, but we updated the contributing guide recommending Node 18 for parity with CI. Release automation (semantic-release) was tested in dry-run mode and no changes to release metadata were introduced.

Related: ENG-4821 (CI stability), ENG-4820 (build perf), SUP-993 (support flake incident), referenced older PR pr-18420-ci-deps-node16-workflow-refactor for historical context.

review_comments: Alice Chen: Nice consolidation. Please add a short note in CONTRIBUTING.md describing how to run the new reusable workflows locally (eg. act or Docker-based local runner).
Jordan Lee: Added CONTRIBUTING note and a small 'local ci' section pointing to scripts/ci-helpers.sh — PTAL.
Marco Alvarez: The deterministic cache key is good, but can we include package-lock.json hash + node version to avoid accidental Node mismatch? Suggested cache key updated.
Jordan Lee: Updated cache key to include node version and locked file hash. Also added explicit cache hit logging for easier debugging.
Priya Nair: Integration retry looks reasonable. One small nit: prefer 3 retries with exponential backoff instead of fixed intervals. Applied the change in the last commit.
Alice Chen: Approved after docs update and a successful CI run.
release_notes: CI: upgrade workflows to Node 18, add reusable workflow templates, improve cache keys for faster cold builds, pin devDependencies used in CI helpers. Non-functional/infrastructure change.
notes: Initial run had one flaky integration test; rerun fixed the failure. Cache improvements reduced average cold CI time from ~12m to ~7.5m on ubuntu-latest images. Contributors should use Node 18 for parity; CONTRIBUTING.md updated.
